name: Anshu Chimala
role: Former Apple eng/design leadership · YC founder · AI design educator
bio: Anshu Chimala led software engineering and design teams at Apple for about 12 years, focusing on research and prototyping for future AI products. A YC founder, he posts AI design tutorials and demos on X and writes deeper craft notes on Substack. His guest essay in Lenny’s Newsletter (Sep 2026) maps an end-to-end process for tapping AI’s hidden creativity—loosely inspired by the Double Diamond, reimagined for a team of AI agents: Discover, Define, Deliver.

stages.title: Discover
stages.summary: Explore beyond average slop—vary directions and write bold, ambitious briefs before going deep.

stages.title: Define
stages.summary: Push past familiar patterns. Chain models, critics, images, and motion until the design has an individual identity.

stages.title: Deliver
stages.summary: Polish with restraint: cut clutter, kill AI tells, and rewrite the words that matter by hand.

highlights: Eight techniques · Discover → Define → Deliver for a team of agents.
Seed strings + ambitious briefs to escape SaaS-landing priors.
Critic subagents, image/video enrichment, then subtractive Deliver polish.
Primary source: Lenny’s Newsletter guest essay (Sep 2026); techniques 7–8 deeper detail paywalled.

name: Greg Huntoon
role: Manager, Designer Advocates · Figma · TC-EBC prompt framework
bio: Partial catalog from Greg Huntoon’s public Figma blog post “Cooking with constraints” and the TC-EBC reference repo. TC-EBC (Task, Context, Elements, Behavior, Constraints) structures prompts so LLM-driven design tools get clear intent instead of polite ambiguity. Earlier stub mistakenly listed David Kossnick here; authorship of TC-EBC is Greg’s. No endorsement.
highlights: Mise en place for prompts: clarity, context, constraints before heat hits the pan.
Polite fluff dilutes intention—models need clean instructions.
Revision discipline: put do-not-adjust rules in Constraints.
Five techniques catalogued (partial)—skeletons from the public post only.

stages.title: Discover
stages.summary: Task and Context lock what you’re building and for whom before Elements sprawl.

stages.title: Define
stages.summary: Elements and Behavior turn inventory + interaction into a buildable prompt.

stages.title: Deliver
stages.summary: Constraints hold the rails—especially what not to change on revision passes.

name: Nate Parrott
role: Product designer at Anthropic · built Claude Design
bio: Partial catalog from one public Claude blog post (no endorsement). Nate Parrott, a product designer at Anthropic who built Claude Design, describes using it to explore, iterate, and share visual ideas early—prototypes, decks, animations—before committing to build. This entry catalogs his published best practices and “make it alive” craft notes from that article only; it does not invent unpublished material.

links.label: Claude blog: exploring ideas before building

stages.title: Discover
stages.summary: Front-load intent, wireframe structure, sketch the indescribable, and generate many options to remix.

stages.title: Define
stages.summary: Specify look, bake brand into a design system, ground work in real product context, and make artifacts alive.

stages.title: Deliver
stages.summary: Point-and-talk edits, finish the last mile by hand, and keep collaborating without waiting on every turn.

highlights: Eleven practices from one public Claude Design post (partial).
Think before you prompt; specify look; system from assets; ten options then remix.
Sketch, point-and-talk, wireframe-first; last mile manual; real context; work alongside.
Make it alive — Bret Victor’s dead-fish warning as craft north star.
